2. The opposite party No.1 as plaintiff filed the above suit for declaration that the appointment of defendant No.2 as Chairman of the Managing Committee of Raipur Pilot Boys High School pursuant to Memo No.30/Laksmi/319 dated 14.5.07 is illegal, impropriety, void and not binding upon him and also further declaration that the plaintiff is still chairman of the said school. On 27.5.07 during pendency of the suit, the plaintiff filed an application for injunction Under Order 39 Rule I read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure restraining the defendant No.2 from performing the function as Chairman of the Managing Committee of the said school and not to interfere with the plaintiff in performing function as chairperson of the School Managing Committee and also stay operation of the impugned memo. It was objected by the defendant Nos. l and 2 by filing written objection. 

 3. By the order dated 29.11.2007 the learned Assistant Judge rejected the application and refused to grant injunction in favour of the plaintiff. 

 4. Being aggrieved there against, the plaintiff preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.01 of 2008 before the Court of District Judge, Lakshmipur, who by the impugned judgment and order allowed the appeal and granted temporary injunction in favour of the plaintiff. 

 6. Although this matter was fixed up at the top of the list subject to part heard matter on an application filed by the opposite party-plaintiff with due service of the copy of that application upon the learned advocate for the petitioner and the matter appeared in the list with the name of the learned advocate for the petitioner on several dates but no one appears to press this rule, which shows that the petitioner has lost his interest. 

 Considering this circular it appears that it is only applicable to the chairman and member of the governing body, who have been nominated on political consideration only. It appears from the impugned judgment that the learned District Judge found that the petitioner is a elected chairman of the governing body and the said election held, long after the said circular was published and as such the said circular is not applicable to the instant case of the petitioner and thus the impugned memo through which the plaintiff was removed and U.N.O. was appointed as a chairman of the Managing Committee is per-se illegal and thus found a prima facie case of the plaintiff and passed an order of injunction in his favour. Considering the aforesaid memo, I found the learned District Judge committed no illegality in passing the impugned order. Since the plaintiff has got a prima facie case the learned District Judge has rightly granted temporary injunction in this favour.
